title: Financial due diligence workbench: data ingestion, trial balance mapping and first-draft databook
problem: Financial due diligence starts with collecting, checking and adjusting data before anyone can interpret it, and a large share of junior time goes there.
approach: An AI platform reads unstructured deal information, structures the data and drafts first-pass outputs; Forvis Mazars US cites trial balance mapping.
Forvis Mazars Group says its rollout of Opio's platform uses embedded controls, full traceability and mandatory human review.
Opio reports 27% average time saved per engagement (vendor-published); Forvis Mazars Group says quality and depth improved after testing (self-reported).

title: Transaction-level anomaly scoring and flux analysis to prepare management meetings
problem: Preparing for the first management meeting is a bottleneck: teams comb thousands of trial balance rows to find movements worth asking about.
approach: A module scores each transaction for anomaly risk, flags movements against user-set thresholds, and tracks candidate EBITDA adjustments to raise with management.
Audit Sight says the module eliminates 80% of prep time for the management-meeting step (vendor-published).
A Miller Cooper principal says the tool shaved days off the deal cycle (self-reported, unquantified).
The deal team tracks flagged adjustments and prepares management questions; who decides which flags become adjustments is not stated.

title: Proof of cash and bank-to-ledger reconciliation by AI agents for smaller deals
problem: In lower-middle-market deals the seller's books are often thin, and reconciling thirty-six months across several accounts from scans takes weeks of work.
approach: QoEAgent's agents read bank statements, including scans, tie revenue and expenses to the bank, and map the trial balance to GAAP financials.
QoEAgent says proof of cash reconciles within 1% in 24 hours; one engagement matched 99.4%, with one $32 variance flagged (vendor-published).
In one described engagement, the proof of cash found unrecorded deferrals and the buyer walked away before closing (vendor-published).
CPAs and M&A advisors review every flagged item and own every conclusion; software does extraction and matching.

title: AI-suggested EBITDA adjustments with source-linked evidence for reviewer sign-off
problem: Adjustments from reported to normalized EBITDA decide the price, and finding, supporting and tracing them in spreadsheets is slow and hard to audit.
approach: Shepi's platform surfaces adjustment candidates, links each to supporting records where available, shows gaps, and produces a PDF and Excel package.
The vendor says every conclusion is linked to source evidence so reviewers can trace a number to its origin (vendor-published, no figure).
The user approves or rejects each adjustment; in the Done-For-You tier a licensed CPA reviews adjustments before delivery.

title: AI-native quality-of-earnings service tiers priced below a traditional engagement
problem: Small and lower-middle-market buyers must choose between an expensive traditional engagement and fragile spreadsheet work.
approach: QoEAgent sells scoped tiers from cash review to full QoE; Shepi lists Self-Service at $1,000 per project and Done-For-You at $5,000 (vendor-published).
A Columbia team posted that its custom model cuts production cost significantly even with an accountant verifying (self-reported, no figure).
A licensed CPA reviews adjustments in Shepi's Done-For-You tier; credentialed professionals own conclusions at QoEAgent.

title: White-labelled AI quality-of-earnings capacity for transaction advisory and CPA firms
problem: Transaction advisory and CPA firms need extra capacity for proof-of-cash and trial-balance work during busy periods.
approach: QoEAgent says it white-labels or supports parts of engagements, from proof of cash and trial balance mapping through the databook.
Shepi pitches accountants on extra capacity; its Firm Edition offers white-label deliverables and resale at custom pricing. No outcome figure is published.
Where QoEAgent works behind a CPA or transaction advisory firm, that firm is the provider and signs the report.

title: AI-assisted lender quality-of-earnings reports for small-business acquisition loans
problem: An SBA rule effective 2026-10-01 makes an independent quality-of-earnings report with a cash proof a condition on larger acquisition loans; QoEAgent says this adds weeks to every deal.
approach: QoEAgent offers an SBA Lender QoE built to the rule: cash proof, GAAP financials, adjusted EBITDA schedules and customer analysis.
No speed or accuracy figure is published.
A named professional stands behind the conclusions, with lender vendor review where a buyer-commissioned report is used.

title: AI-assisted sell-side quality-of-earnings and pre-sale diligence readiness
problem: Sellers who wait for the buyer's diligence meet findings late, mid-process, which can trigger price adjustments.
approach: Pease Bell describes running AI-driven pre-sale diligence and a sell-side QoE with proof of cash before going to market.
Pease Bell says this reduces the likelihood of purchase price adjustments and speeds the path to closing (self-reported, no figure).
Human checkpoints are not described.

title: Data-room document intelligence with source citations for diligence teams
problem: Data rooms are growing and timelines compressing, making it harder to bring the same judgment to each issue; contract review was often descoped from financial diligence.
approach: Tools ingest data rooms, surface key points with source citations and let teams question documents; PwC Deals used ToltIQ on live transactions.
PwC's deals GenAI leader says contracts once descoped can now be reviewed, which creates follow-up on anomalies.
PwC and ToltIQ report 4,000+ PwC Deals practitioners, 5,000+ deals and 2 million+ documents (self-reported).
Practitioners review the anomalies AI flags; an illustrative 20 hours of human follow-up is given.

title: Deeper-cut analytics using time freed from routine diligence
problem: Forvis Mazars US says automating routine work lets diligence teams dive deeper, and that one identified EBITDA adjustment can be worth many times the fee.
approach: Forvis Mazars US says automating the routine frees time for SKU-level data, customer and vendor insight, employee productivity and working capital trends.
It says depth of analysis increases (self-reported, no figure).
Professional judgment stays on EBITDA quality, net working capital, debt-like items and what matters to the deal.

title: Lifecycle M&A platform with an agent harness, from diligence to integration
problem: Deloitte contrasts connected workflows across the deal lifecycle with addressing isolated M&A tasks, in deals that carry tax, technology and financial complexity.
approach: Deloitte's M&A Platform embeds AI across the deal lifecycle, supported by an agentic harness, with workflows from strategy and diligence through integration.
Deloitte says it is in use across more than 1,000 client engagements (self-reported); EY-Parthenon markets a comparable Diligence Edge platform.
Deloitte's survey of 500 leaders reports 66% automated status reporting and 60% enhanced decision-making (vendor-published).
Deloitte describes the platform as human-led and AI-powered.

title: AI-drafted diligence deliverables: QoE exhibits, summary slides and red-flag reports
problem: Turning workpapers and databooks into exhibits, summary slides and red-flag reports is specialist work; no source measures the time it takes.
approach: PwC UK's Deals CTO describes producing executive-ready summaries from complex workpapers (secondary summary).
A July 2026 expert-network posting says an AI lab wants advisory managers to create and refine AI-generated QoE exhibits and red-flag reports.
Experienced transaction advisory managers evaluate and refine the AI-generated pages. No speed figure is published.
who: PwC UK (secondary), an AI lab posting

title: Buyers and sponsors run first-pass diligence with generative AI in-house
problem: Private equity and corporate deal teams must evaluate more opportunities and larger information volumes on tight deadlines, so some first-pass diligence moves in-house.
approach: Deal teams use AI in diligence themselves: S&P Global finds 31% of respondents report AI integrated into due diligence (independent).
Datasite and FT Longitude report 50% of dealmakers regularly use AI in diligence; SS&C Intralinks reports 21-30% time saving (vendor-published).
Human review and validation remain; 45% say the decision to sign should always remain human.
who: S&P Global, Datasite, SS&C Intralinks, Deloitte

title: Post-deal integration planning, transition agreements and synergy sizing with generative AI
problem: Post-deal value realisation needs coordinated execution across systems and is less structured and harder to scale than pre-deal analysis.
approach: Bain expects early adopters to draft integration workplans and transition service agreements in less than 20% of prior time (vendor-published).
Bain also expects them to use company data to size synergies and draft value creation plans.
Deloitte's survey reports 52% apply or pilot GenAI in post-close integration; Accenture reports 27% investing in 2026, up from 18% in 2024.
Human review remains the top requirement for high-stakes use.

title: Language-model knowledge capture to retain, not replace, an acquired company's systems
problem: Post-merger systems integration often threatens the human and IT-embedded knowledge of the acquired firm; the first acquirer chose to rip out and replace the target's ERP.
approach: In a study of two acquisitions of one target, the second acquirer used language-model chat to learn and retain its proprietary ERP.
The authors report increased knowledge transferability and efficiency, and lower assumed system opacity, personnel dependence and conversion cost (independent).
Human checkpoints are not discussed in the abstract.

title: Idea: autonomous quality-of-earnings analysis
problem: Idea, not a deployment: quality-of-earnings work is judgment-heavy and takes weeks, and surveyed dealmakers see an agent that runs the whole analysis as a coming disruption.
approach: An agent would run the analysis end to end with human checkpoints; surveyed dealmakers discuss it, but it is no deployed product.
A July 2026 buyer's guide says no AI tool runs a full QoE because it turns on judgment.
Human checkpoints are not specified.
